title: A Second Passover and a Guiding Cloud
overview: Israel keeps the Passover in the desert, makes room for people who could not take part on time, and learns to travel only when the cloud over God's tent moves.

parts.label: Passover at Sinai (vv. 1-5)
parts.note: Passover was the yearly meal remembering Israel's escape from Egypt, and here it is held one year after that night, while the people are still camped in the desert. They follow the instructions exactly.

parts.label: A problem after a death (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: Touching a dead body, even to bury a relative, made a person ritually unclean, meaning unfit to take part in worship for seven days. Some men caught by this ask why they should miss out, and Moses does not guess but says he will ask the LORD.

parts.label: A second chance date (vv. 9-13)
parts.note: Anyone unclean or far away on a journey could keep Passover a month later with all the same rules, including not breaking the lamb's bones, a detail Christians later read as pointing to Jesus's death. But someone who simply chose to skip it faced being removed from the community, a serious penalty whose exact form scholars are unsure of.

parts.label: Same rule for foreigners (v. 14)
parts.note: A foreigner living among Israel could join the Passover under the same rules as anyone born Israelite. Other passages add that men first had to be circumcised, which marked them as joining the community.

parts.label: Cloud and fire (vv. 15-16)
parts.note: From the day the tabernacle, the portable worship tent, was set up, a cloud covered it and glowed like fire at night. It was understood as a visible sign that God was present with them.

parts.label: Moving when the cloud moved (vv. 17-23)
parts.note: When the cloud lifted, the whole camp packed up, and when it settled they stayed, whether for one night or a whole year. The repetition stresses that their timing came from the LORD, not from their own plans or restlessness.

think: When have you had to wait without knowing how long it would last, and what made that waiting easier or harder to bear?
